name: Washington

sales.rateNote: State retail sales tax of 6.5% (RCW 82.08.020) plus a local rate that varies by city and county. Washington is destination-based: the rate is that of the place where the customer receives the goods or services.

scheduledChanges.what: ESSB 5814: advertising, IT services, custom website development, custom software, live presentations, security and investigation services and temporary staffing became subject to retail sales tax.
Additional motor vehicle sales/use tax rose from 0.3% to 0.5%; new 8% luxury tax on vehicles priced over $100,000.
Additional tax on retail car rentals falls from 11.9% (2026) to 9.9%.

local.levies: cities, counties, transit authorities and other special districts
local.capNote: No single overall local cap published by the Department of Revenue; local rates vary by location.

groceries.note: Food and food ingredients are exempt (RCW 82.08.0293); prepared food, soft drinks, bottled water and dietary supplements are taxable.

otherRates.item: motor vehicles (additional motor vehicle sales/use tax)
otherRates.note: On top of the regular sales tax; 0.3% through December 31, 2025, 0.5% since January 1, 2026.
8% on the part of the price above $100,000 (deduction raised 2% each July 1), on top of sales tax and motor vehicle tax, since January 1, 2026.
11.9% from January 1 to December 31, 2026, then 9.9% from 2027, in addition to sales tax.
Additional 0.5% on the retail sale of recreational vessels.

sales.holidayNote: Washington has no sales tax holiday.

useTax.note: Use tax (state plus local) is paid by the consumer when retail sales tax was not collected by the seller.

facts.text: Since October 1, 2025 (ESSB 5814), many business services are taxed: advertising, IT support and consulting, custom websites and software, security services, temporary staffing and live presentations.
Telehealth and telemedicine are now specifically excluded from retail sales tax.
Buying a car over $100,000 now costs an extra 8% luxury tax on the amount above $100,000: on a $150,000 selling price plus a $50,000 trade-in, it applies to $100,000.
Bottled water and soft drinks are taxable even though groceries are exempt.
Retail services such as repairs, cleaning and installation for consumers have long been taxable in Washington.

property.levied: state school levy plus local levies (counties, cities, school districts, fire, library and other districts); collected by county treasurers

assessment.text: County assessors appraise all property at 100% of its true and fair market value, according to its highest and best use. The state constitution limits regular (non-voted) levies on a property to 1% of market value ($10 per $1,000); voter-approved levies come on top.

homestead.name: No general homestead exemption
homestead.text: Washington has no general homestead exemption for all owners. Relief is income-based: an exemption for seniors (61+), people with disabilities and certain disabled veterans, plus deferral programs.

otherRelief.name: Senior citizens and people with disabilities exemption
otherRelief.text: For owners aged 61+, retired due to disability, or veterans rated 80%+ or totally disabled, with combined disposable income at or below the county's Income Threshold 3; the reduction depends on income, home value and local levy rates. Renewal at least every six years.

otherRelief.name: Deferral for seniors and people with disabilities
otherRelief.text: Owners 60+ or disabled can defer taxes and special assessments at 5% simple interest, repaid on sale or death.

otherRelief.name: Deferral for limited-income homeowners
otherRelief.text: Owners of five years with combined disposable income of $57,000 or less can defer the October half; apply by September 1.

otherRelief.name: Assistance for widows/widowers of veterans
otherRelief.text: Grant toward property taxes for qualifying surviving spouses of veterans, within the county income threshold.

dueDates.text: First half due April 30 and second half due October 31 (taxes under $50 must be paid in full by April 30). Late taxes accrue 1% interest per month, and a 3% penalty applies if still delinquent on June 1.

facts.text: Each taxing district can raise its regular levy by only 1% a year, plus revenue from new construction and improvements: a $1 million levy can become $1.01 million.
Official example: a $150,000 home at a levy rate of $9.41 per $1,000 owes $1,411.50.
Property tax accounts for about 30% of total state and local taxes in Washington and was the first tax levied in the state.
Senior exemption income thresholds are set by county; thresholds for 2027-2029 were updated under ESSB 6162.
Paying 2024 taxes on December 31, 2024 meant 8% interest plus an 11% penalty, per the Department's example.

uncertain: State rate: no change to the 6.5% state retail sales tax rate was found in 2025-2026 (RCW 82.08.020 still reads six and five-tenths percent).
Whether local sales taxes also exempt groceries is based on the local taxes following the state base; not read explicitly.
The date the 6.5% rate took effect was not verified.
